description: Hungarian-domiciled banks that issue bonds but sit under foreign parents (K&H/KBC, Raiffeisen Bank Zrt., CIB, Erste Bank Hungary as opposed to its mortgage bank) were only partially explored in this pass.
Earnings-call audio/transcripts for OTP were only located via a gated third-party aggregator; the issuer's own conference-call recordings/transcripts page was not pinned to a specific URL.
The MNB OAM (kozzetetelek.mnb.hu) search/query interface and any bulk or per-issuer listing endpoint were not mapped; only the download URL pattern was observed.
BÉT's per-issuer 'Közzétételek' tab URLs and any RSS/news feed for KIB disclosures were not captured as concrete endpoints.

Payments-specific disclosure (card/POS/acquiring volumes, instant-payment metrics) inside these issuers' reports was not separately located; it is likely embedded in segment sections of annual reports and investor presentations rather than in dedicated documents.

The cell as seeded covers eight institutions, but the foreign-owned unlisted population in Hungary is larger (e.g. other Zrt.-model and fióktelep-model lenders and consumer-finance houses not named in the seed).
For several institutions only document-level PDFs are known, not the durable index page a monitor should watch for new filings.
Discovery surfaced mostly recent documents (roughly 2015-2025 for UniCredit, 2020-2025 for Raiffeisen, 2017-2024 for CIB). Historical depth and completeness per entity is unmapped.
The two most authoritative pointer sources (e-beszámoló and kozzetetelek.mnb.hu) both use opaque ids / form-driven search rather than crawlable indexes; neither was exercised end-to-end in this run.

Slovak/German/Korean/French parent-level disclosures (KBC, Erste Group, RBI, UniCredit SpA, Intesa Sanpaolo, Oberbank AG, KDB, Cofidis SA) that segment-report Hungary were not scouted, as they fall outside this cell.

Hungarian chambers of commerce (MKIK national, BKIK Budapest) and their financial/economic sections were not covered; likewise other foreign bilateral chambers with financial committees (German-Hungarian DUIHK, British, French chambers).
The two highest-value registers in the cell — hunfintech.com/hu/tagok/ and ivsz.hu's member directory — were located but not enumerated, most likely because the listings are JavaScript-rendered.

No search was run for the cooperative-credit and specialist-lender bodies (e.g. takarékszövetkezeti integráció, building-society/lakástakarék bodies, Magyar Követeléskezelők adjacents already partly covered), nor for the Hungarian Association of Investment Fund and Asset Management Companies (BAMOSZ) or the Budapest Stock Exchange issuer community.

English-language coverage in this cell leaned on supranational bodies (EBF, Leaseurope, EPC, AmCham). The English mirrors of the Hungarian association sites (lang=eng) were inferred from URL patterns rather than confirmed, so EN/HU content parity is unknown.
The GVH decision search is a dynamic interface; whether full decision texts are downloadable as PDFs from result pages was not established, and no test query on a banking entity was executed.

Association member lists are published as current-state pages with no visible historical versions, so membership churn (entries, exits, mergers) cannot be reconstructed retrospectively from the sources themselves.

This cell's outlets cover BANKING earnings well but payments-specific Hungarian trade coverage (card schemes, acquirers, POS, instant payment/AFR, PSD2/e-money issuers) was not surfaced. No dedicated Hungarian payments trade title was identified.

The cell rationale relies on the press as a timestamp/archive layer for unstable filing URLs, but nothing was established about how long these outlets keep articles addressable, whether they have public archives or sitemaps, or whether they are captured by web archives.

The premise that Hungarian press surfaces figures for foreign-owned subsidiaries with no English release (Erste Hungary, K&H, CIB, Raiffeisen, UniCredit Hungary, Gránit, MagNet, Cofidis) is supported by sector-aggregate articles but was not tested entity by entity.

MTI (Hungarian news agency) appears to be the upstream of much identical bank-results wording across portals, but MTI itself and its OS (press-release distribution) service were not scouted in this cell.

Only one substantive English-language trade outlet (BBJ) was identified for this cell; Portfolio.hu is described as having an English edition but no English bank-earnings URL was surfaced in this run.
Non-bank payment actors — Barion, OTP Mobil/SimplePay, Revolut Hungary, Wise, PayU/Shoptet Pay, Diákhitel, Posta/MPT — have no confirmed press channel in this slice.
RSS/Atom endpoints and corporate LinkedIn/YouTube newsrooms are unmapped across the whole cell.
English-language twins of Hungarian press rooms were only confirmed for CIB and MNB; for OTP, MBH, K&H, Erste and Raiffeisen the en/ paths are assumed rather than observed.

PR agency wires serving Hungarian finance were only partially mapped: three agencies were identified via Helló Sajtó! but their bank/PSP client rosters were not enumerated, and no other HU PR wire (beyond MTI OS and Helló Sajtó!) was identified.
Archive depth per newsroom is unknown; only OTP (year-partitioned /ir/kozlemenyek/{year}), MNB and GVH showed evidence of multi-year archives.

Per-entity rating pages for K&H Bank, CIB Bank, Raiffeisen Bank Zrt., UniCredit Bank Hungary, Gránit Bank and Eximbank were not individually located in this pass; only aggregate references were found.
Which Big4 firm audits which Hungarian bank, and the history of auditor rotation (mandatory rotation applies to public-interest entities), was not established.

The individual atlathatosagi jelentes (transparency reports) that KPMG Hungary, Deloitte Hungary, PwC Hungary and EY Hungary must publish on their own websites within 3 months of year-end were not located as URLs in this pass.
No archival/back-file strategy was established for rating actions predating ESMA ERP's 1 July 2015 start, or for withdrawn ratings on merged entities (MKB, Takarék, Budapest Bank pre-MBH).
Redistribution rights for agency text (Moody's/Fitch/S&P/Scope) inside an internal intelligence product were not established.
The BÉT YouTube channel is documented by BÉT itself as carrying conference/education video, but the exact channel handle/URL was not confirmed in this pass.

No independent aggregated Hungarian analyst-consensus dataset (outside OTP's own issuer-published consensus) was identified — e.g. no public HU equivalent of a consensus vendor page for MBH or other listed financials.

Cell coverage skews to banks/issuers; no sell-side or investor-event source specific to the PAYMENTS side (acquiring, POS, card schemes, fintech) was found in HU. Payments appears only obliquely via Portfolio's Financial IT / Future of Finance conference agendas.

Regional broker investor conferences that host Hungarian bank management (WOOD's Prague/Winter conferences, Erste Group's Stegersbach/CEE conference, Concorde's own investor events) were inferred but not individually located with agenda URLs.

English-language coverage of the domestic broker layer is thin: Concorde, Erste Befektetési and Equilor publish predominantly in Hungarian, so an EN-only collector would miss the entire domestic sell-side stream.

The legacy-entity list whose IR estates need archival recovery is not yet enumerated beyond MKB, Budapest Bank and Takarekbank - other wound-down or absorbed HU institutions (savings-cooperative brands under the Takarek umbrella, Sberbank Magyarorszag, Commerzbank Zrt., MagNet/Granit predecessor brands) are unmapped.

No verification was done of how deep Wayback's captures actually go for mkb.hu, takarekbank.hu and budapestbank.hu IR sub-paths, nor whether the PDFs themselves (not just the index pages) were captured.

PSP/fintech-specific aggregators and archives were only partially covered - the EBA PSD2 register is captured, but national-register mirrors used by payments-industry vendors, and archives of retired Hungarian PSP sites, were not explored.

Closed-collection access to the OSZK Webarchivum and commercial licence terms for Opten/D&B/EMIS/Orbis are unresolved, so the realistic collection method for a large part of this cell is currently unpriced.

English-language normalisation of HU bank filings is available almost exclusively through paid aggregators; among free sources only the EBA datasets, ECB lists and BET/issuer English pages provide it, and statutory filings on e-beszamolo and the MNB OAM are Hungarian-only.

No parent-IR source identified for Hungarian consumer-credit and payments players whose parents are outside the six named groups — notably Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale / Cofidis (now owning Magyar Cetelem) and any remaining foreign-owned niche lenders.

Digital and payment-specific KPIs (card counts, mobile banking users, transaction volumes, acceptance/acquiring) for Hungary were only indirectly evidenced — RBI's net-commission commentary on clearing/settlement/payment services was the strongest signal found; no parent slide with a Hungary payments KPI table was located in this pass.

Capital Markets Day / strategy-update material was not covered. Multi-year Hungary strategy (branch footprint, digital investment, acquisitions) is usually revealed at CMDs rather than in quarterly reports.
Webcast/audio and issuer-hosted transcripts for the parents' quarterly calls were not located as direct URLs; only third-party transcript mirrors with ToS/bot-defence issues were found.
No URL in this slice was fetched or liveness-tested; all entries rest on search-result evidence. Several rest on CDN-token paths known to rotate.
The OAM issuer/entity category indexes were not enumerated in this pass, so the actual count and identity of HU banking/payments filers on kozzetetelek.mnb.hu remains unknown.
Savings-cooperative / integration successor entities (Takarék, MBH group members), KELER/KELER KSZF and GIRO Zrt. filing footprints were not individually traced in this cell.
Robots.txt, terms of use and rate-limit posture were not checked for kozzetetelek.mnb.hu, e-beszamolo.im.gov.hu, bet.hu or intezmenykereso.mnb.hu.
English mirrors were confirmed to exist for MNB OAM, Intézménykereső and bet.hu, but their completeness relative to the Hungarian originals was not assessed.
Historical archive depth is unknown for the OAM, Cégközlöny online and bet.hu issuer news.

The interactive Aranykönyv and the Intézménykereső are JavaScript applications; the underlying data endpoints, file naming and pagination were not inspected in this pass (only their landing pages were identified).
Release timing for the Aranykönyv, quarterly credit-institution tables and payment statistics was not confirmed; MNB publishes a statistical release calendar that was not located in this pass.

It is unconfirmed whether the Aranykönyv datasets and the Intézménykereső register share a stable institution identifier (MNB registration number, or LEI/company registration number) that would let per-bank financials be joined to licence records.
MNB's terms of use / reuse conditions and robots.txt for mnb.hu, statisztika.mnb.hu and intezmenykereso.mnb.hu were not read in this pass.
English mirrors exist for the Golden Books, supervisory statistics and pressroom, but registers, decisions search and most recommendations appear HU-only.

The full population of licensed Hungarian pénzforgalmi intézmények and elektronikuspénz-kibocsátó intézmények was not enumerated in this pass; only the well-known brands were reached. The MNB register was identified but not harvested.

Passported EU providers serving Hungary (Wise Europe SA, Revolut Bank UAB, Zen.com if applicable, Stripe, Adyen, PayPal) file little or nothing locally, so their Hungarian business is invisible in HU filings.

Fintech corporate news in this cell is substantially English-first (PayU, Revolut, Wise, SEON, Pay10) while statutory disclosure is Hungarian-only. This pass covered HU heavily and EN only lightly, so English-language issuer blogs and newsrooms are under-sampled.

Social and non-web channels were not scouted: LinkedIn company pages, X/Twitter, YouTube conference talks and podcast appearances are where several Hungarian PSPs first state volume and customer numbers. Only one Facebook page surfaced incidentally (B-Payment).

No Hungarian fintech/payments industry association or sector-report publisher was confirmed in this pass (e.g. a national fintech association, MNB fintech reports, Big Four Hungarian payments studies).
Filing history depth and retention on e-beszámoló for these entities was not established, nor whether older press-centre items remain reachable after site redesigns.

GIRO's English-language disclosure footprint was not established. Only Hungarian-language repository content was confirmed; whether an English annual report or English scheme documentation exists is unknown.

KELER Group ownership and its shareholders' own reporting (MNB majority, Budapesti Értéktőzsde / BSE minority) were not traced. BSE annual reports would carry a KELER equity-method line and post-trade commentary.

CSDR Article 26 / EMIR public quantitative disclosures and PFMI self-assessments for KELER and KELER KSZF were not individually located, though the disclosure obligation makes their existence near-certain.
No archival/time-machine strategy was established for versioned scheme documents (BKR Üzletszabályzat, Díjszabályzat, Posta Pénzforgalmi Üzletszabályzat), which are overwritten at the canonical URL.

Adjacent Hungarian clearing/collection infrastructure (e.g. the Díjbeszedő group and its bill-payment clearing role, and any card-scheme domestic processing entity) was not investigated and may belong in this cell.

No fetch was attempted against keler.hu, kelerkszf.hu, posta.hu, mnb.hu or e-beszamolo.im.gov.hu in this pass; only giro.hu was fetched. All other URLs come from search-engine results and are therefore unverified for liveness.

No source located for card-scheme domestic interchange fee schedules published for Hungary (Mastercard/Visa country interchange PDFs), which is where the regulated economics of Hungarian acquiring is actually stated.

Processor actors with Hungarian back-office/processing operations beyond the named five were not explored (e.g. FIS/Worldpay, Diebold Nixdorf, ACI, Tietoevry, and card personalisation/processing bureaus with Budapest sites).

Hungarian-language terminology for the acquiring/processing layer was harvested (kártyaelfogadás, elfogadóhely, elfogadói hálózat, elfogadói üzletág, POS terminál, bankkártya-elfogadás, sajtóközlemény, éves beszámoló) but no Hungarian term set was established for scheme-side concepts such as interchange, scheme fees or tokenisation.
No archival/wayback strategy captured for the corporate press rooms in this cell, which routinely reorganise URLs (Visa.hu numeric slugs, Worldline deep paths, SIX legacy estate).

Exact Hungarian legal-entity names and registration numbers were confirmed only for Nexi Hungary Zrt. and Visa Europe (Hungary) Kft.; the Worldline/SIX and Global Payments Hungarian entities were not pinned down, blocking a complete e-beszamolo pull.
Cardtronics (now part of NCR Atleos) as a distinct Hungarian ATM estate operator was not separately evidenced; only Euronet's HU estate is documented.
No vendor recruitment/job-ad sources were scouted, although HU-language job posts (profession.hu, LinkedIn) routinely name the bank a vendor is staffing a project for.
The inter-bank ATM obligation delegation contracts mandated by MNB 19/2025 (min. 5 years, deadline 2025-07-31) are referenced in media but no repository of the contracts themselves was located.
Municipal council documents proved to be a high-value direct source but only one example (Onga) was found; there is no systematic index across ~3,150 HU settlements.
Branch cash-automation OEMs (Glory, Giesecke+Devrient, CIMA, SUZOHAPP/Cashtec) and their HU distributors are largely unmapped.

The full population of Hungarian szakosított hitelintézetek and pénzügyi vállalkozások in this cell was not enumerated in this pass; only named/seeded actors were covered. Dozens of smaller licensed lenders remain unlisted.
Post-consolidation reporting of individual former takarékszövetkezetek and the Integrációs Szervezet (SZHISZ) was not investigated; only MTB's group-level archive was found.
The e-beszamolo beszámoló kereső is form/POST driven and its programmatic accessibility (rate limits, CAPTCHA, KAÜ requirement for search vs. submission) was not tested in this pass.
Rating agency and supranational-lender reporting on Hungarian promotional banks (Scope, NEFI, EIB/EBRD counterparty disclosures) was only touched incidentally via one Scope rating report link.

State-owner-side reporting (MNV Zrt., Ministry of National Economy ownership reports, parliamentary submissions on MFB/EXIM) was not searched, though these often contain performance data not in the banks' own reports.
